value.summary: CR-142 adds two things to the layered FastAPI/SQLAlchemy URL shortener: client-chosen aliases (3-32 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, reserved words give 422, a taken alias gives 409) and optional link expiry (`expires_at`, which must be in the future; redirecting an expired link gives 410; metadata reports `is_expired`). The change touches the create flow: the LinkCreate schema, LinkService.create_link (the code-retry loop, the IntegrityError mapping and the idempotency request hash), code-format checks used by lookup, redirect, stats and delete, the redirect 410 logic, the response schemas, and the `links` table (new nullable `expires_at` DATETIME column). No column change is needed for aliases because `code` is already String(32) with UNIQUE uq_links_code. The schema change has to be explicit because `Base.metadata.create_all` never alters existing tables and there is no migration tooling (OPERATIONS.md says so). If the column is not added on an existing database, every query on `links` fails with 503. BUG-77 investigation: `validate_target_url` (app/schemas/links.py) is correct for both claims. It lower-cases the scheme via urlsplit before checking it against {http, https}, so `HTTP://Example.com` is accepted and stored unchanged. Any `javascript:` URL fails the scheme check (with or without `//`), and leading whitespace or control characters are rejected first. The existing parametrised tests (HTTPS://, HtTp://, javascript:alert(1), JAVASCRIPT://example.com/%0aalert(1)) and the doctest pass: I ran `pytest tests/test_create_and_validation.py --doctest-modules app/schemas/links.py`, exit 0. The baseline suite of 165 tests passes. The URL validator does not reproduce the reported behaviour, so no fix is needed there. Regression tests should still be added for the exact reported inputs and for case and whitespace variants of `javascript:`. Likely explanations for the report: a 401 from the newer API-key auth, input with surrounding whitespace or newlines (rejected by design), or rows written directly to the database (no validation at redirect time). Related real defects found: the reserved list is missing `metrics`; the API.md, OPERATIONS.md, README and CHANGELOG security notes wrongly say there is no authentication; and the existing tests pin `is_valid_code_format` to base62 only, which matters for alias lookup.

architecture.responsibility: create_app() factory plus module-level app. Builds Settings, engine and session factory on app.state, registers JSON exception handlers and request-logging middleware, runs Base.metadata.create_all in lifespan startup (creates missing tables only, never ALTERs), and includes routers in the order health, links (/api/links), then the redirect catch-all /{code} last.

Management router /api/links, protected by the require_api_key dependency on the whole router: POST create (201, Location header, Idempotency-Key header, Idempotent-Replayed), GET /{code} metadata, DELETE /{code} soft delete, GET /{code}/stats. Maps service results to Pydantic response models.
Public catch-all GET /{code} (307 with exact Location, Cache-Control: no-store, records a click) and HEAD /{code} (no click). Raw Response is used to avoid re-quoting the URL.
DI providers: get_settings (from app.state), require_api_key (constant-time X-API-Key check, fails closed), get_link_service and get_stats_service (built per request from get_db), build_short_url.
GET /healthz (liveness, no DB) and GET /readyz (SELECT 1, 503 on failure).

Pydantic v2 models: LinkCreate (url: StrictStr plus the validate_target_url validator), LinkCreatedResponse, LinkDetailResponse (adds deactivated_at, total_clicks), stats models, ErrorResponse. Hosts URL validation and the _as_utc helper (naive values treated as UTC). The architecture test forbids importing other app packages here.

Business rules and transaction ownership (the only module that commits or rolls back): create_link (Idempotency-Key handling, request_hash = sha256(url), retry loop over generated codes that discards reserved codes and treats IntegrityError as a collision, 503 on exhaustion), _get_or_404 (format check, then DB lookup), get_link_detail, deactivate, resolve_for_redirect (HEAD), resolve_and_record_click (410 if inactive, best-effort click insert).

generate_code (secrets, base62), RESERVED_CODES with case-insensitive is_reserved, CODE_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,32}$ in is_valid_code_format. Used by link_service and stats_service to reject malformed codes with 404 before querying.
Per-link analytics (total, clicks_per_day in a UTC window, top referrers). Uses codes.is_valid_code_format and LinkRepository.get_by_code.
get_by_code (select by code) and add (add plus flush; IntegrityError propagates). Never commits.
get_by_key and add for IdempotencyKey rows (flush only).
Click event insert and aggregate queries (count, timestamps since, referrer counts).
ORM Link (table links): id, code String(32) with UNIQUE uq_links_code, url String(2048), is_active, created_at, deactivated_at. Datetimes are naive UTC.
ORM IdempotencyKey: key String(255) UNIQUE, request_hash String(64), link_id FK to links.id, created_at.
ORM ClickEvent: link_id, created_at, referrer, user_agent, ip_hash. Index (link_id, created_at).
DeclarativeBase Base and utcnow() returning naive UTC.

Framework-agnostic AppError hierarchy (400/404/409/410/503; no 422 domain error exists) and JSON handlers for AppError, HTTPException, RequestValidationError (422 with a list detail), SQLAlchemyError (503) and unhandled exceptions (500). No stack traces are leaked.
pydantic-settings Settings: database_url, base_url, short_code_length, code_max_attempts, ip_hash_salt, log_level, api_key.
create_db_engine, create_session_factory, and get_db (request-scoped session, the single test override point).
JSON log formatter and request-logging middleware (method, path, status, duration; never the client IP).

165 passing tests (99.19% coverage). conftest.make_client builds an isolated app on a fresh temporary SQLite database per test with an API key. test_config_openapi_architecture enforces layering (schemas cannot import app.*; core cannot import services), portable sqltypes, text() with literals only, pinned requirements, and OpenAPI schema names.

impacted_files.reason: Add `expires_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(DateTime, nullable=True)` (naive UTC, portable sqltypes.DateTime). `code` String(32) already fits 32-char aliases and keeps UNIQUE uq_links_code, so no other column change. Optionally add a helper property such as `is_expired_at(now)`, keeping the models layer free of app.* imports.

Explicit schema migration is needed because create_all does not ALTER the existing `links` table. Suggested: an idempotent `ensure_schema(engine)` that uses sqlalchemy.inspect to check for the `expires_at` column and, if missing, runs the literal DDL `ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at DATETIME NULL` (one literal string, so test_sql_text_only_receives_literal_strings stays green; portable across SQLite, Postgres and MySQL).
Call the migration step in lifespan after Base.metadata.create_all. Router order stays the same (catch-all last).

LinkCreate: add optional `alias: str | None` (format ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$, 422 on failure) and optional `expires_at: datetime | None` (ISO-8601; naive treated as UTC via _as_utc; must be in the future, else 422). Consider strict parsing so numbers are not coerced to timestamps. LinkCreatedResponse/LinkDetailResponse: add additive fields `expires_at: datetime | None = None` (UTC-normalised) and `is_expired: bool`. Existing fields are unchanged. The reserved-word list cannot be imported from app.services here (architecture test), so either duplicate the list in schemas or check reserved words in the service with a 422 domain error.

Add `metrics` to RESERVED_CODES (required by the CR; also blocks generated codes). Keep `is_valid_code_format` base62-only because tests/test_codes.py asserts `not is_valid_code_format('abc-123')`. Add new helpers instead, e.g. `ALIAS_PATTERN`/`is_valid_alias` (3-32, [A-Za-z0-9_-]) and `is_valid_lookup_code` (1-32, [A-Za-z0-9_-]) for path lookups.

create_link(url, idempotency_key, alias=None, expires_at=None, now=None). With an alias: run reserved and format checks (422), skip the generated-code retry loop, and map IntegrityError on code to ConflictError 409 ('Alias already in use'), not a retry or 503. Store expires_at as naive UTC. Extend request_hash to cover alias and expires_at while keeping sha256(url) when both are absent, so existing stored keys still replay (backwards compatible). _get_or_404 must use the widened lookup-format check so links with '-' or '_' aliases resolve. resolve_for_redirect and resolve_and_record_click must raise a 410 for expired links (expires_at <= utcnow) with a distinct detail such as 'Link has expired', and record no click. LinkDetail/CreateResult or the API layer must expose is_expired (use an injectable clock for testability).

get_stats uses codes.is_valid_code_format and would return 404 for stats of aliases containing '-' or '_'. Switch it to the widened lookup check. Stats should stay available for expired links, as they are for deactivated ones.

Add a 422 domain error (e.g. UnprocessableEntityError, status_code=422) if reserved, alias or expiry rules are enforced in the service layer. Optionally add an expired-link detail constant; GoneError's default detail is 'Link has been deactivated', which is wrong for expired links.

create_link passes payload.alias and payload.expires_at to the service and returns the new response fields. get_link adds expires_at and is_expired. OpenAPI `responses` needs updated 409 (alias taken) and 422 (reserved or invalid alias, past expires_at) descriptions.
Document 410 for expired links in the responses metadata. Behaviour comes from the service (GET and HEAD both return 410 for expired links; no click on GET).

New tests: valid aliases (boundaries of 3 and 32 chars, '-' and '_') get 201 and can be redirected, looked up, deleted and queried for stats; 2 or 33 chars or bad characters get 422; reserved words (api, docs, redoc, healthz, readyz, metrics, openapi.json, case-insensitive) get 422; a duplicate alias (also against deactivated or expired links, and on an IntegrityError race) gets 409 with nothing persisted; idempotency with an alias (same key with a different alias gives 409, same payload replays).

New tests: expires_at in the future gets 201 and the field is echoed; past or now gets 422; naive vs offset datetimes normalise to UTC; redirect after expiry (controlled clock or direct DB update) returns 410 JSON with no Location and no click; HEAD returns 410; metadata shows is_expired true/false; stats still work; links without expires_at never expire.

BUG-77 regression tests: `HTTP://Example.com`, `HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM/Path` get 201 and are stored unchanged. `javascript:alert(1)`, `JavaScript:alert(1)`, `JAVASCRIPT:alert(1)`, `javascript://example.com/%0aalert(1)`, ` javascript:alert(1)`, `\tjavascript:alert(1)`, `java\nscript:alert(1)`, `http:javascript:alert(1)` get 422 with zero rows. Docstrings should cite BUG-77.

Start the app against a SQLite file created with the pre-CR-142 `links` schema (no expires_at) containing a row. Startup must add the column; the old link still redirects with 307, its metadata shows expires_at null and is_expired false, and new links can be created.

Document alias/expires_at request fields, the expires_at/is_expired response fields, new 409/410/422 cases, the widened `{code}` lookup format ([A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}), the request_hash change, and the reserved list. Also fix the stale 'Authentication: none' statement (API key is enforced).
Data model table (links.expires_at), the explicit migration step (automatic ALTER or manual SQL for DBAs), idempotency request_hash definition, and the stale 'No authentication' security note.
Add [Unreleased] entries for CR-142 (aliases, expiration, schema change) and BUG-77 (investigated; regression tests added).
Feature list and security notice (says 'no authentication', which is stale).

apis_affected: POST /api/links: new optional body fields `alias`, `expires_at`; new 409 (alias taken) and 422 (reserved/invalid alias, non-future expires_at); response adds `expires_at`, `is_expired` (additive)
GET /api/links/{code}: response adds `expires_at`, `is_expired`; must resolve aliases containing '-'/'_'
GET /api/links/{code}/stats: must resolve aliases containing '-'/'_'; available for expired links
GET /{code}: 410 Gone for expired links (no click recorded); resolves aliases
HEAD /{code}: 410 for expired links; resolves aliases
GET /openapi.json: LinkCreate/LinkCreatedResponse/LinkDetailResponse schemas gain fields (schema names unchanged)
data_model_changes: links: ADD COLUMN expires_at DATETIME NULL (naive UTC, generic sqlalchemy DateTime). Existing rows get NULL, meaning they never expire.

links.code: no DDL change. Already VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL with UNIQUE uq_links_code, which enforces alias uniqueness (case-sensitive on SQLite/Postgres; case-insensitive under MySQL default collations).

idempotency_keys.request_hash: no DDL change (still 64-char hex), but its meaning widens. It stays sha256(url) when alias and expires_at are absent (compatible with stored rows) and becomes a hash of a canonical url+alias+expires_at payload otherwise.

Migration: create_all does not alter existing tables, so an explicit idempotent ALTER TABLE step (or documented manual SQL) is required. Optional: an index on expires_at is NOT needed (it is only read per-row on lookup).
data_flows: Create: POST /api/links -> require_api_key -> LinkCreate validation (url via validate_target_url, alias format, expires_at future/UTC) -> LinkService.create_link (Idempotency-Key lookup/replay by request_hash -> alias path: reserved check + single insert, IntegrityError -> 409 | generated path: retry loop) -> LinkRepository.add (flush) -> IdempotencyRepository.add -> commit -> LinkCreatedResponse (+expires_at, is_expired), Location header

Redirect: GET /{code} -> LinkService.resolve_and_record_click -> lookup-format check -> LinkRepository.get_by_code -> inactive => 410 / expired (expires_at <= utcnow) => 410 -> ClickRepository.add best-effort -> 307
HEAD /{code} -> LinkService.resolve_for_redirect -> same 404/410 checks, no click
Metadata: GET /api/links/{code} -> LinkService.get_link_detail -> LinkDetailResponse with expires_at/is_expired computed against current UTC
Stats/Delete: StatsService.get_stats / LinkService.deactivate -> lookup-format check (must accept alias charset) -> get_by_code
Startup: create_app lifespan -> Base.metadata.create_all -> NEW explicit migration adding links.expires_at to pre-existing tables
regression_areas: Existing create flow: generated 7-char base62 codes, collision retry, reserved-candidate discard, 503 exhaustion (tests/test_codes.py patches app.services.codes.generate_code, so the retry loop must keep calling codes.generate_code)
codes.is_valid_code_format must stay base62-only (test_codes asserts 'abc-123' is invalid). Malformed-code tests (abc-def, abc_def, a.b, 40 chars, percent-encoded) must still return 404 JSON.

Idempotency: same key + same url replays an identical body (now including expires_at/is_expired; must be deterministic); different url gives 409; race handling; stored request_hash rows must keep matching url-only requests
Redirect: 307 exact Location not re-quoted, Cache-Control no-store, 410 for deactivated links with detail string, HEAD records no click, 404/410 record no click, best-effort click recording
Response shapes: existing fields of LinkCreatedResponse/LinkDetailResponse unchanged; created_at/deactivated_at UTC 'Z' normalisation
Probes /healthz, /readyz and docs routes not shadowed (router order); reserved words keep those paths unreachable as codes
API-key auth on /api/links* (router dependency) applies to new behaviour as well

Architecture/static tests: schemas import nothing from app.*, core doesn't import services, models use only portable sqltypes, text() only with literal strings, pinned requirements, OpenAPI schema names
URL validation behaviour (BUG-77): accepted/rejected sets in test_create_and_validation.py and the doctest
Performance NFR-4 (redirect p95 < 50 ms, create p95 < 100 ms): the expiry check must add no extra query
Startup against existing databases (tables created before the change)

existing_defects.description: BUG-77 not reproducible: upper-case schemes ARE accepted and `javascript:` URLs ARE rejected by the current validator. No code defect in URL validation; regression tests are still required.
existing_defects.evidence: `parts.scheme.lower() not in _ALLOWED_SCHEMES` (urlsplit already lower-cases the scheme) accepts HTTP://Example.com and rejects any javascript scheme. `_is_forbidden_char` rejects leading or embedded whitespace and control characters before parsing, and `value[len(parts.scheme):].startswith('://')` rejects `http:javascript:`. Existing tests test_valid_urls_are_accepted ('HTTPS://example.com', 'HtTp://example.com/path') and test_invalid_urls_return_422_and_persist_nothing ('javascript:alert(1)', 'JAVASCRIPT://example.com/%0aalert(1)') pass, as does the module doctest. Plausible causes for the report: 401 from the X-API-Key requirement, whitespace or newlines around the pasted URL (rejected by design), or rows inserted directly into the DB, since redirect does not re-validate stored URLs.

existing_defects.description: Reserved-word list lacks `metrics`, which CR-142 requires to be reserved. Today a generated code `metrics` would be accepted, and a future /metrics route would be shadowed by or conflict with such a link.

The code-format check used for every lookup only allows base62, so links with aliases containing '-' or '_' would be unreachable (404) for redirect, metadata, delete and stats unless a widened check is used. tests/test_codes.py pins the existing function's behaviour, so a new function is needed rather than editing CODE_PATTERN.
existing_defects.location: app/services/codes.py:CODE_PATTERN / is_valid_code_format; used in app/services/link_service.py:_get_or_404 and app/services/stats_service.py:get_stats

existing_defects.description: Idempotency payload hash covers only the URL. Once alias and expires_at exist, reusing a key with the same url but a different alias or expiry would silently replay the original link instead of returning 409.
existing_defects.evidence: The hash input is `url` only, and _replay_or_conflict compares only record.request_hash. docs/API.md: 'The payload is compared by the SHA-256 hash of the `url` string.'

existing_defects.description: Every IntegrityError on link insert is treated as a generated-code collision and retried, ending in 503 'Could not allocate a unique short code'. For a client-chosen alias this would produce wrong statuses (retries with random codes, or 503) instead of 409.
existing_defects.location: app/services/link_service.py:create_link retry loop (`except IntegrityError: self.session.rollback(); continue`)
existing_defects.evidence: The for-loop over max_attempts always calls codes.generate_code and `continue`s on IntegrityError; it ends with `raise ServiceUnavailableError(...)`.

existing_defects.description: No schema migration mechanism: startup only runs create_all, which does not add new columns to existing tables. Adding links.expires_at without an explicit migration breaks every links query on existing deployments (503).
existing_defects.evidence: OPERATIONS.md: 'Existing tables are **not** altered, and there is no migration tooling in this release.' requirements.txt has no alembic.

existing_defects.description: GoneError's default detail is specific to deactivation, so reusing it for expired links would return a misleading message.
existing_defects.evidence: default_detail = "Link has been deactivated"; resolve_for_redirect and resolve_and_record_click raise GoneError() with no detail.

existing_defects.description: Stale documentation says the management API has no authentication, but it is enforced by an API key (require_api_key, fail-closed).
existing_defects.location: docs/API.md ('Authentication: none in this release'), docs/OPERATIONS.md Security notes, README.md line 11, CHANGELOG.md 1.0.0 Security
existing_defects.evidence: app/api/links.py router has `dependencies=[Depends(require_api_key)]`; tests/test_auth.py covers 401 behaviour.

risks.description: Existing databases lack links.expires_at; create_all won't add it, so all link queries fail with 503 after deploy.
risks.mitigation: Add an explicit, idempotent migration (inspect, then a literal `ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at DATETIME NULL`) run at startup after create_all, plus manual SQL in OPERATIONS.md. Add a test that boots the app on a pre-CR-142 SQLite file. Concurrent multi-instance startup could race on ALTER; document 'migrate once first' or tolerate 'duplicate column' errors.

risks.description: Changing the idempotency request_hash formula breaks replay of keys stored before the change (409 instead of replay).
risks.mitigation: Keep sha256(url) when alias and expires_at are both absent; only use a canonical extended payload when they are present. Test that a pre-existing key/url pair still replays.

risks.description: Widening the lookup format by editing CODE_PATTERN breaks tests/test_codes.py (abc-123 must be invalid), violating 'existing tests must keep passing'.
risks.mitigation: Add a separate lookup/alias validator in codes.py and use it in _get_or_404 and StatsService. Leave is_valid_code_format unchanged for generated codes.

risks.description: The alias uniqueness race and the generated-code retry share the IntegrityError path; misclassification yields 503 or a random code instead of 409.
risks.mitigation: Separate branch for the alias path: one insert attempt, IntegrityError leads to rollback and ConflictError (409). Pre-check get_by_code for a friendly 409 but rely on the unique constraint for races. Test with a monkeypatched race.

risks.description: Timezone handling: DB stores naive UTC; clients send offset-aware or naive ISO strings. Mixing aware and naive values raises TypeError (500) or shifts expiry by the UTC offset. 'Must be in the future' is evaluated at request time.
risks.mitigation: Normalise to aware UTC in the schema (naive treated as UTC, as _as_utc does), convert to naive UTC before persistence, compare against models.utcnow(), and make the clock injectable in the service. Return UTC 'Z' in responses.

risks.description: Reserved-word check placement: schemas cannot import app.services (architecture test), so duplicating the list risks drift between generated-code and alias reserved sets.
risks.mitigation: Single source of truth in codes.RESERVED_CODES (plus 'metrics'), enforced in the service with a 422 AppError. Or, if validated in the schema, add a test asserting both lists are equal. Reserved matching stays case-insensitive (is_reserved uses casefold).

risks.description: Case-sensitivity differs by backend: under MySQL default collations, 'MyLink' and 'mylink' collide (409) and lookups match case-insensitively, while SQLite/Postgres treat them as distinct.
risks.mitigation: Document it. Optionally specify a binary collation for links.code on MySQL in a later change. Keep tests on SQLite semantics.

risks.description: Adding computed `is_expired` to create and replay responses could make idempotent replays differ from the original body if the link expires in between, and expiry checks could slow down the hot redirect path.
risks.mitigation: Compute is_expired from the already-loaded row (no extra query). Document that replays reflect current state, as is_active already does. Keep the NFR-4 performance test green.

risks.description: Pydantic lax datetime parsing accepts integers or loose formats for expires_at, beyond the ISO-8601 contract.
risks.mitigation: Use strict or ISO-only parsing (e.g. a string field with a before-validator, or a Strict datetime in JSON mode) and test that numeric input gives 422.
